title: The Strongest Sacrifice
html:
Thirty minutes later, all the grade-6 monsters had been dealt with.

Our efforts, particularly Gong Pildu's ability to fight large armies, had been extremely effective.

It was a moment that made taking in one of the 10 Evils worthwhile.

“······We can finally catch our breath. You said the next wave comes in four hours, right?”

Lee Jihye spoke as she tucked her long sword into her belt.

Looking around, I saw that the fighting nearby was also dying down.

I didn't know about the other areas, but we had at least defended Gangseo.

Of course, not everyone had escaped unharmed.

“Dad! Please, wake up! Dad!”

“Someone, please help!”

Most incarnations who still lacked the know-how to hunt grade-6 monsters hadn't even managed to put up much resistance. Some had suffered severe injuries after being struck by a [Heavy Hound]'s forepaw; others had died when their internal organs burst. Most were incarnations who had only recently been brought in.

[ * Current number of incarnations: 90,531 ]

Only the first wave had passed, yet a tenth of the Seoul Dome had died.

A little distance away, Yoo Joonghyuk was watching the incarnations.

Watching him made me a little uneasy.

The dokkaebi had said:

Through the sacrifice of the single strongest incarnation, every incarnation in the Seoul Dome could survive.

“Hey, Yoo Joonghyuk.”

Yoo Joonghyuk turned toward me.

I didn't know exactly what that sight meant to him.

As I kept saying, reading ‘Ways of Survival’ didn't mean I truly knew everything about its characters. In the end, what I could understand was the text, which had already been shaped once before it reached me.

And some things became unreadable precisely because I could read them.

“Let's talk for a minute.”

●

We went up to the rooftop of a nearby high-rise.

On the way, I used ‘Character List’ on Yoo Joonghyuk for the first time in a while.

[The exclusive skill, ‘Character List’, activates.]

[There is too much information about this character. ‘Character List’ will be converted to ‘Summary List’.]

[Only arbitrarily selected fields will be displayed for the user's convenience.]

●

<Character Summary List>

Character: Yoo Joonghyuk

Constellation Sponsor: ???

Exclusive Attributes: Regressor <3rd Round> (Myth), Pro Gamer (Rare), Supreme King (Hero)

Exclusive Skills: [Sage's Eye Lv.9], [Hand to Hand Combat Lv.10], [Advanced Weapons Training Lv.10], [Advanced Mental Barrier Lv.3], [Hundred Steps Godly Fists Lv.9], [Red Phoenix Shunpo Lv.8], [Splitting the Sky Energy Lv.8]······(omitted)······.

Stigmas: [Regression Lv.3], [Transmission Lv.5]

●

I still couldn't see who his ‘constellation sponsor’ was.

I already knew why it wasn't visible.

Even in the original ‘Ways of Survival’, Yoo Joonghyuk's sponsor had never been revealed.

I'd thought the sponsor might appear in the epilogue, but unfortunately, I hadn't been able to read the epilogue of ‘Ways of Survival’.

A constellation with greater resistance to ‘probability’ than any constellation I knew, and the power to turn the wheel of time and deceive even other constellations. A constellation that never once gave Yoo Joonghyuk a stigma other than ‘Regression’, all the way to the end of ‘Ways of Survival’······.

Even I couldn't say for certain what kind of being it was, or what it hoped to gain through Yoo Joonghyuk.

“······You have a way to kill Nirvana?”

Honestly, the bastard was impatient.

He'd finally been given time to rest, and that was the first thing on his mind.

Even with Regression Depression, Yoo Joonghyuk was still Yoo Joonghyuk.

“Let's catch our breath first. The view's nice, too.”

I spoke as I perched on the rooftop railing.

Yoo Joonghyuk asked through what sounded like gritted teeth.

“······What are you plotting?”

“Just take a look at the world. Isn't it beautiful?”

The view before us was of Seoul, devastated by monsters.

I hastily added,

“It used to be beautiful, at least.”

“I don't like scenery.”

“Why?”

“Because it will all disappear someday.”

I'd thought the battle against Shin Yoosung had helped me understand the third-round Yoo Joonghyuk a little better. I wanted to believe he might be someone who didn't give up or despair so easily, someone who knew how to love this world a little more.

“But these are the things you have to protect.”

“Kim Dokja, you know nothing.”

But perhaps I'd misunderstood him.

Because there were things Yoo Joonghyuk refused to let go of through countless regressions, there were also things he could abandon at any moment.

Ultimately, Yoo Joonghyuk's goal was ‘to prevent this world's destruction’.

Paradoxically, to achieve that goal, he ‘could abandon this world at any time’.

At his core, he was a regressor. That fact wouldn't change.

“No, I do know.”

“What?”

“Being able to regress whenever you want must mean ‘death’ has no meaning.”

Below the rooftop, I could see Lee Seolhwa tending to the injured.

Lee Seolhwa, giving a nameless character a medicinal brew she'd prepared.

But regardless of her efforts, that character would most likely die. Even if they survived now, they would die tomorrow; even if they miraculously survived tomorrow, they would die the day after.

In the fourth round, and in the fifth.

Even beyond the hundredth round, in Yoo Joonghyuk's world, they would always be ‘people who were already dead’.

“But if death has no meaning, life loses its value, too.”

“What the hell do you know······?”

“Yoo Joonghyuk, get a grip. I'm telling you not to fool yourself into thinking things will get better if you repeat them a few times.”

Perhaps startled by my forceful words, Yoo Joonghyuk fell silent for a moment.

“Sure, you might do better in the fourth round than you have now. But you might not. You haven't already forgotten the ‘Theatre Dungeon’, have you? If I hadn't shown up then, you would've—”

“Things will improve with each round. There were many unexpected events this round, but the next will certainly be better again.”

“Why? Because you'll know more about the future?”

Yoo Joonghyuk fell silent.

There was probably some agreement in that silence.

Part of ‘Ways of Survival’ flashed through my mind.

Was it around the forty-eighth round?

An incarnation sponsored by the constellation ‘Discoverer of the Unconscious’ had once counseled Yoo Joonghyuk about his ‘Regression Depression’.

I thought that person had probably said something much like what I was saying now.

“All right. Maybe you're right. If you repeat this for ten or twenty rounds, things could certainly improve little by little. You'll encounter more scenarios and see more futures. But the real problem comes when you eventually save this world that way.”

“······What do you mean?”

“When that happens, do you think you'll really be able to believe you ‘saved this world’?”

“······.”

“I'm asking if you'll still be able to think that after regressing a hundred or two hundred times.”

“There's no way I'll regress that many times.”

I looked at Yoo Joonghyuk without a word.

「······Surely not?」

Yoo Joonghyuk's eyes slowly widened.

I continued.

“You still have nightmares, don't you?”

“······.”

“Even if you save the world, you won't be saved. The moment you save it, the worlds you abandoned will come crashing down on you. Even if you save one world, all the other worlds you abandoned will drag you into hell.”

For a brief moment, Yoo Joonghyuk's gaze wavered violently.

He'd probably had some vague awareness of it himself.

“So live ‘this round’ properly. Shin Yoosung broke after wandering through countless years. But if you keep going through round after round, those endlessly repeating rounds will break you beyond repair. Ask yourself. How different are you now from the person you were at the beginning?"

"That's······."

Yoo Joonghyuk's expression stiffened.

I could see his gaze wavering violently.

After all, even Yoo Joonghyuk couldn't have been like that from the start.

"Don't fool yourself into thinking the next round will be better just because you abandon this one. This round you're trying to abandon might be the ‘one and only round’ in which you can see this world through to its end as a 'human being'.”

“······.”

Yoo Joonghyuk kept his mouth shut.

Intense conflict surfaced on his face, as though he wanted to say something but couldn't get the words out.

That's right, Yoo Joonghyuk.

Struggle with it.

And don't regress.

If you regress, what becomes of me?

[The character ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ recovers a small amount of mental strength.]

As though he'd reconsidered something, a faint glimmer of resolve crossed Yoo Joonghyuk's face.

Life in this goddamn world would be hard either way.

There was nothing to do but pick yourself up and live on with every last ounce of strength. Perhaps he'd come to think that if he had to live, he could only give it his all while he was alive.

A cool breeze blew in from somewhere, and we looked down together at the ruins of Seoul as it washed over us.

“This scenario is more like a special event. Things will return to the course we knew. We can make full use of the future again. There must be plenty of hidden pieces left that only you know about, right? If we can just free the ‘Seoul Dome’ somehow······.”

Just then, the rooftop door opened with a creak, and our companions came tumbling through. Gong Pildu was the first to land facedown on the floor, with Lee Jihye and the children sprawled on top of him.

“Aaargh! Stop pushing!”

“Come on, I want to know what they're talking about. Why do you get to listen all by yourself, ajusshi?”

“You don't just barge into a conversation between men.”

“Men, my ass······.”

······I had a pretty good idea what had happened.

[The eyes of the constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ sparkle.]

“What were you two doing······?”

I cut Lee Jihye off before she could spout more nonsense.

“No stupid jokes today. I'm not in the mood.”

[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is crestfallen.]

Crestfallen or not, Yoo Joonghyuk mattered more to me right now than a constellation.

Uriel didn't have to give me any more coins. I wished she'd just go to Jung Heewon.

Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.

“We were discussing a strategy for the scenario.”

“A strategy? What kind of strategy?”

At that, Yoo Joonghyuk looked at me.

“This scenario ends only when the strongest incarnation dies. I was thinking about that.”

A shiver ran down my spine.

Why was this bastard looking at me as he said that?

Lee Jihye asked, sounding a little excited.

“Oh, we were just talking about that ourselves. So what did you decide? Who's the strongest incarnation?”

“Me, of course.”

Watching Yoo Joonghyuk answer with such confidence, I realized my worry had been misplaced.

Well, with that much pride······.

No, hold on.

The strongest incarnation had to die for this scenario to end, and he'd been thinking that was him······.

“Were you actually planning to die?”

“If I die, we can stop this scenario.”

I was a little moved by his noble intentions.

Damn it, his <Regression Depression> suddenly seemed kind of cool.

But I couldn't actually let him die.

“Aren't you getting ahead of yourself? There's no guarantee you're the strongest, is there? There's me, for instance······.”

At my words, all my companions turned to look at me.

Lee Jihye slapped my shoulder and gave an exaggerated laugh.

“Come on, you can't be serious.”

“Dokja-hyung, that's a bit······.”

Lee Gilyoung looked at me with pity, while Shin Yoosung looked confused, as though she still wasn't sure.

Even Gong Pildu and Min Jiwon had something to say.

“That's not even worth asking.”

“······Wouldn't the Supreme King still be stronger?”

“Wait, ajusshi, are you saying that because you beat the Salvation Church's leader earlier?”

She'd hit the nail on the head.

“But there's no way you beat them because you're actually strong, right? I didn't see it, but I bet you used some weird trick. Am I wrong?”

In a way, she was right, so I had nothing to say.

Feeling somehow relegated to the sidelines, I added what sounded like an excuse.

“······I was just giving an example. What I mean is that the Salvation Church's leader might be stronger than Yoo Joonghyuk. He actually had a pretty hard time earlier.”

Lee Jihye's eyes widened in apparent surprise.

“Is that true, Master?”

“······They're a bad matchup for me.”

Yoo Joonghyuk's remark threw the group into confusion.

“Then······could the Salvation Church's leader be the strongest?”

“Oh my god, there's a human stronger than Master?”

“But what exactly are the rankings based on? Combat strength? Or is whoever actually wins a fight considered stronger······?”

I answered Min Jiwon's question.

“For now, I suspect there's some numerical measure of ‘overall combat strength’. Everyone can't fight everyone else, after all. The rankings might change after a fight determines a winner and a loser, though.”

“Come to think of it, didn't the dokkaebi say something like that earlier? That ‘the strongest incarnation would know best’······.”

We looked toward Yoo Joonghyuk again.

“Yoo Joonghyuk, has anything been different from usual? Did a dokkaebi say something to you, for instance?”

Yoo Joonghyuk slowly clenched and unclenched his fist as he spoke.

“······Well, I haven't heard anything.”

I turned to the others.

“It seems nothing is certain yet.”

“Then what do we do now?”

“Let's take that as a good thing. No one here wants Yoo Joonghyuk to die, do they? For now, I think the reasonable choice is to assume Nirvana is the ‘strongest’ and take them down.”

“But if it turns out the Supreme King is the strongest······.”

“We'll think about that when the time comes.”

Min Jiwon spoke.

“The Salvation Church is north of the river. Security is tight, so even getting close won't be easy, and they vastly outnumber us. Even if we all go······.”

“We won't go. We'll call them to us.”

“How? Would they agree? No matter how I look at it, there's no way they'd do something that puts them at a disadvantage······.”

“That's what common sense would suggest.”

But Nirvana wasn't someone with common sense.

The monsters were coming from the outskirts of Seoul.

Gates were probably forming there, and the monsters' grades would rise sharply at four-hour intervals.

In other words, we had eight hours left at most.

Within that time, I had to lure Nirvana out and make them face Yoo Joonghyuk.

“I think I have a way.”

Leaving my companions, I called Bihyung through ‘Dokkaebi Communication’.

But the voice that answered belonged to Youngki.

[I'm sorry. Bihyung-nim is a little busy right now······.]

That bastard Bihyung. It seemed promotion season was coming up, and this was how he was going to act?

Who did he think had gotten him where he was? Ungrateful bastard.

I'd been planning to boost his sales for the first time in a while, but he was kicking his own good fortune away.

—The special random boxes for the new scenario are out, right?

[Yes. They're available.]

—I'll buy ten.

I'd expected Youngki to jump at the chance to sell them, but surprisingly, Youngki hesitated.

[But the odds for the random boxes are terrible······. Are you sure?]

—It's fine. Sell them to me.

What on earth was that dokkaebi bastard worrying about?

Would this one be able to survive, acting like that?

[You have purchased 10 ‘Main Scenario # 8 Special Random Boxes’!]

[You have spent 30,000 coins.]

—You can go now.

[Yes. Then may the blessing of stories be with you.]

Youngki's voice faded, and ten sparkling boxes descended from thin air. Colorful boxes with large question marks printed on them.

Lee Gilyoung, who was beside me, asked,

“Hyung, those are the things from games, right? You open them and randomly get something good······.”

At times like this, kids caught on the fastest.

“Yeah, that's right.”

[Random Box].

A gambling item that offered abysmally low odds of obtaining SSS-grade weapons and SSS-grade skills. This was an item exclusively for suckers, devised by dokkaebis to fleece gullible constellations.

Why had I bought those boxes?

[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ is slightly disappointed in you.]

[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ says integrity is the foundation of a general's character.]

[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ advises you to beware of extravagance.]

[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ wants you to donate to them if you have coins to spend on things like that.]

Min Jiwon's face flushed red at Supreme Maegum's message.

“I-I'm sorry. My sponsor is a bit······.”

“It's all right. They aren't good value for money, to be honest. Anyway, everyone, gather around. I'll give you each one to lift your spirits.”

“You're giving them to us? For free?”

“Yes. But please keep only the main items that come out when you open the boxes. I'd appreciate it if you gave me the consumable bonus items.”

I'd originally considered selling them for coins, but I had built up a certain bond with the people gathered here. If they became stronger, that would help me plenty, too. So this wasn't a deal in which I only stood to lose.

Lee Jihye, whose face lit up at the word ‘free’, was the first to snatch a box.

“Wow, what's gotten into our stingy ajusshi······? I'll put it to good use, ajusshi!”

Gong Pildu and Lee Gilyoung each received a box next.

“Hyung, what if I get an SSS-grade item?”

“The odds are probably less than 0.00001 percent. It'll be pretty difficult.”

“······Really?”

“It's all a marketing trick. Just let yourself get suckered this once and open it.”

Yoo Joonghyuk glared at me intently, then spoke.

“Kim Dokja. You aren't thinking of facing Nirvana with items from those boxes, are you?”

“Well, something like that. Why?”

“······What a pathetic plan.”

He was taking a box himself. This bastard, seriously······.

The last person to take a box from me was Shin Yoosung.

“I'll give you two.”

Shin Yoosung's eyes widened in surprise.

“······Really?”

“Yeah.”

After hesitating for a moment, Shin Yoosung took the boxes from me. Something about her expression seemed unusual, so I took a closer look. Tears were brimming in her eyes.

“Whether I deserve something like this······.”

Only then did I remember young Shin Yoosung's past.

This was probably the first ‘gift’ Shin Yoosung had ever received in her life.

Perhaps for the sake of advancing the plot, that goddamn ‘Ways of Survival’ had plenty of characters with convenient backstories like that.

And what was convenient for someone became someone else's real misery.

I pressed a box into Shin Yoosung's hand as she wiped her eyes.

“Take it. You're my incarnation. You more than deserve it.”

Seeing Shin Yoosung's genuine delight and flushed face made me regret not taking better care of her sooner.

Because I, her sponsor, hadn't yet qualified as a ‘constellation’, Shin Yoosung hadn't received a [Stigma], either.

Had taking this child in been the right choice?

Might I actually be making her unhappy?

For now, I couldn't know.

But I would do everything I could to protect her.

“All right, let's open them. Think of it as a change of pace.”

At my words, everyone nodded and began opening their boxes.

[You have used a ‘Main Scenario # 8 Special Random Box’!]

[You have obtained 2 units of ‘Ellain Forest’s Vital Force’!]

[You have obtained 1 pair of ‘Reasonably Usable Boots (E)’!]

[You have obtained other consumables.]

······Of course. Nothing but consumables and an E-grade item.

It was the same for my other companions.

I'd expected as much. Random boxes were, after all······.

[Congratulations! Someone has beaten the 0.00001% odds!]

Fireworks bursting in midair to a grand celebratory fanfare.

I turned and saw Shin Yoosung looking completely at a loss.

······No way. Really?

“A-Ajusshi?”

A small fruit lay in Shin Yoosung's hand, scattering brilliant light.

When I went closer to inspect it, the item's identity became clear.

Good god. She'd gotten that.

······Just how lucky was my incarnation?

Even Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been watching, seemed a little surprised.

“You got something good.”

An SSS-grade item, [Ancient Beast’s Fruit].

Even among the SSS-grade items that appeared with a 0.00001 percent probability, [Ancient Beast’s Fruit] had the most abysmal drop rate. Although it was a consumable, depending on how it was used, its value could be SSS grade or higher.

“If you feed this fruit to a monster you can't tame, you'll be able to tame it. Congratulations. You should save it for when you need it.”

For Shin Yoosung, who could use [Taming], there was no better item. If she used it on a monster that could evolve into a grade-1 species or higher, the Shin Yoosung of this round might grow to match or surpass her forty-first-round self. Looking back and forth between the fruit and me with sparkling eyes, Shin Yoosung asked,

“Ajusshi, but this······can you only use it on monsters?”

“Probably. Why?”

“······It's nothing.”

Shin Yoosung, who had been looking at me, blushed adorably and avoided my eyes.

Lee Gilyoung, who had been drooling nearby, rushed over.

“Hey, can you give that to me? I'll give you my Titano.”

“I don't like insects.”

Watching them enviously, Lee Jihye spoke.

“Ajusshi, why did you do this, anyway? Was it really just to cheer us up?”

“Of course not. First, give me the consumables you got from the boxes.”

What I'd wanted from the start wasn't the boxes' main items, but the consumables that came as bonuses.

[You have obtained ‘Megaphone (Dome Channel) X 4’!]

[You have obtained ‘Megaphone (General Channel) X 4’!]

[You have obtained ‘Megaphone (Regional Use Only) X 2’!]

Only then did Yoo Joonghyuk narrow his eyes.

“I see what you're planning.”

[Megaphone].

A useful consumable that could send messages to a particular channel or an entire area, depending on its options.

“But there's no way they'll come out over a few words······.”

“What matters is what those words are.”

I used a [Megaphone].

Perhaps I'd start like this.

I began with an opening that would catch Nirvana's attention.

●

At that moment, Nirvana was at the church's temporary headquarters. A statue of Guanyin Bodhisattva looked down with an impassive gaze at Nirvana, who had quietly closed their eyes.

Do not cling to the past, nor resent the future

For the past has already vanished, and the future has yet to come

The verse Nirvana was reciting certainly carried that meaning, but the doctrine did not spread through their voice. Beads of sweat formed on their forehead.

Sharp sparks flew over their entire body. A moment later, their eyes rolled back to show the whites, and a message sounded.

[You have inherited a new skill!]

Only then did Nirvana open their eyes.

“······I overdid it.”

Their stigma, [Succession], consumed a considerable amount of probability when used. Unless they offered the ‘stories’ accumulated through reincarnation to the constellations and received probability in return, they couldn't use [Succession].

‘Too many of my stories were taken.’

Although Nirvana regretted the past they had lost, they soon regained their composure.

To live in the present, there were things one had to empty oneself of.

Gathering their energy, they headed toward the inner sanctum deep within the church. After descending underground for a while, they passed through a corridor and opened a door to a softly lit room.

A room furnished with an antique-style table and a double bed. Decorated with a warmth unexpected in a dank basement, it showed signs of considerable care.

“I've kept you waiting. Shall we begin again today?”

Two women of different ages sat at the table.

They were the missing ‘King of Wanderers’, Lee Sookyung, and Yoo Sangah. Glancing at Yoo Sangah, who sat beside her staring blankly into space with unfocused eyes, Lee Sookyung asked,

“When will you remove the skill you've cast on this girl?”

[Thought Infection].

Several weeks had already passed, yet Yoo Sangah was still resisting.

Nirvana smiled.

“I'm not the one who undoes it. She has to do that herself.”

From Nirvana's perspective, it was intriguing.

“How foolish. All she has to do is declare, ‘I will live in the present’, yet she resists to this extent.”

“The past has a different value to those who live short lives.”

“It is precisely because their lives are short that they should value the present more. Foolish being, blessed with death yet ignorant of its worth.”

“Don't judge someone else's ‘present’ however you please. She's living in the ‘present’ well enough. If anyone doesn't understand the ‘present’, it's you, endlessly repeating the cycle of rebirth.”

“Don't forget. I will keep you alive only as long as your ‘stories’ have value.”

Even at that threat, Lee Sookyung's expression remained composed.

Like Scheherazade in One Thousand and One Nights.

Nirvana slowly approached, pulled out a chair at the table, and sat down.

“There is something I must learn today.”

“What do you want to know?”

“The incarnation named ‘Kim Dokja’.”

For the first time, the smile froze on Lee Sookyung's lips

“He's an incarnation I don't know.”

“There's no use playing innocent. I already know he's your son. That ‘Neutral’ fellow told me.”

“······We were separated when he was young. I know nothing about the life he's lived.”

“We'll know once I look inside.”

A radiant Dharma wheel (法輪) began spinning behind Nirvana.

One of the Thousand Hands of Avalokiteśvara reached out from within the wheel.

The enormous hand settled squarely over Lee Sookyung's head.

Lee Sookyung glared at the hand in apparent disgust.

“Open your memories. Otherwise, the woman beside you will die.”

“What a childish threat.”

“And you have yielded to that childish threat all this time. That is what humans are.”

Lee Sookyung quietly looked at the vacant-eyed Yoo Sangah, then spoke with something like a sigh.

“······Do as you please.”

[Activating the exclusive skill, ‘Dependent Origination (因緣生起) Lv.6’!]

One of the Thousand Hands of Avalokiteśvara dug firmly into Lee Sookyung's head. Her story flowed out and began entangling itself with Nirvana's. This was the sensation of becoming ‘one’. Nirvana trembled at the feeling. Chewing, tasting, tearing, savoring. They were truly feasting on stories, drawing closer to the laws of the <Star Stream>.

“It astonishes me every time. How does a human possess filtered information about the future?”

Lee Sookyung desperately tried to protect her memories, but the fragments of future knowledge she had heard from Kim Dokja couldn't resist the flow of Dependent Origination and were being drawn into Nirvana.

“Interesting. Is this the essence of ‘Kim Dokja’?”

“······.”

“What a sorrowful mother. You lied to your child. To deceive your child about his own life, on your own authority.”

Cold anger surfaced on Lee Sookyung's face.

“You won't be able to beat him.”

“······I'll admit he's an interesting incarnation.”

An incarnation powerful enough to force them to overextend themselves using ‘Succession’.

But only a human. Nothing more.

It was then that a message rang thunderously through the air.

【I challenge the Salvation Church's leader, ‘Nirvana Moebius’, to a duel.】

Startled, Nirvana looked up into the air.

Kim Dokja's megaphone.

As though she'd been waiting for this, Lee Sookyung spoke.

“He's strong and wise. He knows what he needs, and he knows what he does best.”

【The duel will take place at Gwanghwamun at 2 PM today. Your opponent will be the Supreme King, Yoo Joonghyuk. The two closest contenders for the title of strongest will fight and determine who is strongest, thereby protecting the Seoul Dome. If you truly live in the ‘present’, do not avoid this duel.】

To invoke the ‘present’, of all things. If Nirvana truly was the ‘Salvation Church's leader’, this was a duel they couldn't avoid. The cleverness of using an area-wide megaphone was impressive, too. If they avoided the duel, they would face condemnation not only from every incarnation in the Seoul Dome, but also from their fellow Salvation Church members. But walking into an obvious trap was foolish. Nirvana smiled.

“A decent provocation. But what a shame. My goal isn't ‘clearing the scenario’ in the first place. My goal is the great······.”

【Of course, accepting this duel probably isn't part of your ‘great plan’. But.】

At Kim Dokja's next words, Nirvana froze, struck speechless.

【If you come now, I'll give you a chance to become one with ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’.】

Bzzzzzt!

Nirvana was so startled that they lost their hold on the strands of [Dependent Origination] they were using. Amid anger, astonishment, and an inexplicable sense of humiliation, Nirvana trembled all over and bit down on their lip.

Through the strand connecting them, Lee Sookyung felt Nirvana's powerful impulse.

A desire for a greater story, a longing to unite with the great one.

Lee Sookyung smiled as though mocking that desire.

“I told you you'd lose.”

●

【Very well.】

Nirvana's answer came quickly.

Every one of my companions looked stunned, as though they hadn't believed it would actually work.

I stood, shaking my head to clear my swimming vision.

“Dokja-ssi, how did you······? No, more importantly, are you all right?”

Min Jiwon looked worriedly at the dark blue bruise around my left eye.

It was a souvenir from Yoo Joonghyuk hitting me when I'd used his name earlier.

Rubbing my eyelid, I asked,

“Has that bastard already left?”

I'd even been knocked out for a moment.
